note: Every number of the cloud deck. Units are camera heights at the fit of frame 3150 (1 unit = 0.1725 degrees on the sphere). The chart has its origin under the storm, y along the view on the ground, x to the right. maps: the height maps from the finest to the widest, centre and size in units, pixels per side (the web set holds half).

tool.note: Numbers of the tools in assets-src/jupiter/deck that lay the canvas back onto the sphere. heightGain: gain of the depth tool's relief (deck/relief.py), fitted so the storm's walls stand as in the image. reliefSigmaPx: the relief is the depth tool's range over the smooth sphere's range, less its own mean over this many canvas pixels. reliefReach: the relief fades with the range, gone at this many units. depthBlurPx: blur of the image heights in canvas pixels (a map may name its own). resolveFactor, minResolve: the scale the image resolves on the ground is its footprint along the view times resolveFactor, at least minResolve units. trustFrom, trustTo: the image's heights are used where that scale is under trustFrom and not at all over trustTo. heightBlur: least blur of the heights in units (a map may name its own: the fore map holds the ground under the flight at the scale the canvas resolves there, so a crest of the heights stands where the canvas shows it). trustFeather: blur of that trust in units. slopeMax: no stored height may rise faster than this over the ground (a cone is laid over every top and the higher of the two kept), so the march, which sizes a step by the height over the ground and this slope, cannot step over a wall. heightRange: the lowest and highest height the maps store. reliefFade: the heights go to zero from reliefFade[0] to reliefFade[1] units from the point under the fit camera. plateRelief, plateReliefScale: where the image's heights are not used the near map takes the depth tool's relief of the top down near plate, with this gain, less its own mean over plateReliefScale units. roughBand, roughSpread, roughLevel: a plate's alpha is its own roughness, the energy between the scales roughBand in units, spread over roughSpread units, 1 at roughLevel.

canvas.note: The picture the fields are laid back from: the wide canvas of the earlier build (the approved close image in the middle, aprons at the same scale on all sides, recipe in RECIPE.md), with the approved image itself pasted over the middle. scale: canvas size over the size of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the paste fades in. depthShrink: the depth tool runs on the canvas shrunk by this.

core.note: Inside the approved image the fields take their colour from the core: the approved image at scale times its size (the upscale tool, then the fine fold detail of the earlier build, recipe in RECIPE.md under the terrain deck, steps 2 and 11). lockPx: above this many core pixels the core is held to the tone of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the core fades in.

light.note: azimuthDeg: the direction to the Sun on the ground of the chart, measured from the chart's x axis toward its y axis, as the approved image shows it. The function detail is embossed along it and the air is measured about it.

look.note: Numbers of the shader in clouds.ts. shell: lowest and highest height of the layer the march runs in. march: slack added to the slope of the ray when a step is sized by the height over the ground, least step in pixel footprints, a hit counts under this many footprints, most steps. detail: the function detail is a field of rounded tops made per wave length (cells with one seeded top each, each wave turned against the last): the largest wave in units, how much a top is brighter than the crease beside it, a wave may be this many pixels of the canvas at most (the scale the laid back image resolves at that spot, the mean of across and along its view), and this many pixel footprints at least. detailLook: the height a top stands over the mean, power by which a wave's slope falls with its length, least roughness, most change of brightness. detailTone: how much a slope toward the Sun's azimuth lights a top. detailHigh: from above (by the weight of tone.lift) the least wave is this many pixel footprints instead of detail[3], so the function holds a full texel a pixel where a plate is enlarged; the globe draws the same function on the plates of the place. foot: least cosine between ray and ground in the footprint, the footprint is cut into taps when it is longer than this times its width, most taps. blend: share of a height map's half width where it starts to give way to the next and where it ends. join: the same for the plates. trust: the image field is shown fully while the smear of a texel across the pixel's footprint is under trust[0] footprints and not at all over trust[1]; trust[2] = 1 takes the image field away (a check of the plates alone). stretch: a texel may be enlarged this many times before the lookup is widened, most change of tone the plates' own detail may add to a widened lookup (1 = none), most widening, least sine between the fit camera's ray and the ground. anisotropy: taps of the texture filter.

air.note: The air between the camera and the deck, measured by deck/air.py on the approved view: for the plates, which hold the deck as it is from straight above, it gives the share of their light that comes through (by the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground) and the light the air adds (by that sine and by the turn of the ray away from the Sun's azimuth, mirrored). sinRange: the sines of the first and last knot, spaced by ratio. knots: count over the sine, count over the turn from 0 to 180 degrees. clear: between these sines the air ends, so a steep ray sees the plates as they are. minTexels: texels of the view chart a cell needs. smooth: blur of the added light in cells. lift: the air is whole while the camera is lower than the first height in units over the deck and gone from the second, so from far above the plates show as the globe shows them and the air of the approved view comes in as the camera sinks into it.

flight.note: The flight of the surface view. seconds: its length. The camera passes the pose of the approved image at the middle. Forward speed over the ground goes from startUnitsPerSecond to endUnitsPerSecond with the power of the elapsed share. Before the middle it also comes down: startAbove units higher at the start, falling with the sinkPower of the share of the way still to go, so it stays near the bottom plane of the approved view and little ground shows that the image never saw. From the share exposureFrom of the flight to its end the exposure eases by exposureStops, because the sunward cloud that fills more and more of the frame would otherwise lift the frame's mean by a quarter.

view.note: The image field: the canvas laid onto the heights in a chart that matches the view of the fit camera (deck/view.py), so no texel is stretched at the fit pose. Since the fit camera looks its own picture up (image), the chart is seen only where that camera saw nothing or saw the ground too steeply; what it holds there is made by the fill below. thetaDeg: the chart's span of azimuth about the point under the fit camera, from the chart's y axis toward x. psiNearDeg: its nearest ground as the angle of the ray under the horizon. horizonMargin: units of ground distance left out before the horizon. pixels: the size of the chart the geometry is worked out on. fine: the stored chart holds this many texels per such pixel each way. imageMargin: canvas pixels at the canvas border that are not used. Ground the fit camera did not see is found per stored texel by the same test the shader uses (image.hidden against the stored range), so chart and shader agree to the texel. steep: ground whose texel is over this many times longer than on level ground counts as unseen too. Both are filled along the view: the colour of the ground just beyond the gap's far border (the mean of fillMean pixels) runs into the gap and passes to the colour just before its near border, which leaves out hiddenSkip pixels, so a narrow gap is never darker or lighter than both its sides. fillEdge: the outline of the steep ground is smoothed by this many pixels before it is laid on the fine grid. fillSmooth: the distances to the two borders are averaged across the view over this many pixels. fillNear: the ground before the gap (the crest that hides it) is mirrored in only over the last part of the way from the far border to the near one, from this share on; before it the gap holds the far ground alone, which is what a camera ahead of the fit pose sees first. fillAcross: the two border colours are averaged across the view over fillAcross[0] pixels at the border and over fillAcross[1] pixels from fillAcross[2] pixels into the gap on, so a wide gap carries no stripes. fillDetail: the fine structure (what is left of the canvas after a blur of fillDetail[3] pixels) of the ground mirrored about the two borders is added fillDetail[0] times, from fillDetail[1] to fillDetail[2] pixels inside the gap on; nearer to a border the gap is the plain run of colour. fillLength: a filled texel is stored this many times the gap's width longer than level ground where it holds no fine structure, so the shader's own detail fills it at the scale of the pixel. lengthRange: the shortest and longest ground length of a texel the alpha channel stores, by ratio. fade: canvas pixels from the canvas border between which the image field fades out.

limb.note: Glow over the limb as a table over (sunward place of the limb point, tangent height). deck/limb.py measures it on the approved image: python3 limb.py clear, render frame 3150 at the draft tier, python3 limb.py RENDER.png. cover = tangent heights between which the glow stops hiding the sky patch. Rows are spaced by the square root of the height.

plates.note: Top down plates of the place, made from the approved close image by assets-src/jupiter/plates (recipe in assets-src/jupiter/RECIPE.md). Units and chart as the maps; size and pixels are x then y. They hold albedo in the globe's coding (values above white kept), so the globe shows them as the deepest levels of its patches. order: the order in which the plates are made. parents: the plate a canvas is enlarged from; without one the canvas starts from the globe's own albedo at the place, with the flow frozen as in place.json (globeBlurPx: how soft that is in plate pixels). inset: a finished finer plate laid into the canvas at its own place. grade: one colour, the median over the laid back image within gradeRadius units of the vortex of the close image over the globe's albedo, both at a scale of gradeScale units. The plates are the close image divided by it, so they sit on the globe at the globe's own brightness and hue, and the surface view multiplies it back in as one exposure that changes with time alone. useBlur: the laid back image is used where its own blur along the view is under useBlur[0] units, and not at all over useBlur[1]; beyond, near the image's horizon, the globe's own structure stays. flatten: from flatten[0] to flatten[1] units of ground distance from the close camera the laid back image gives up its tone above a scale of flatten[2] units to the globe's, because there its tone is the haze of a low view, not the cloud. carry: outside the laid back image the canvas carries the image's tone on from the border (measured at a scale of carry[0] units) and lets it go over carry[1] units. free: outside the laid back image the repaint is tied to the canvas at a scale that grows by this many pixels of blur per pixel of distance from the border. softPx: plate pixels of blur per unit of the image's own blur along the view, which marks unresolved parts as unfinished for the repaint. parentBlurPx: the blur of a level enlarged from the level above. clear: the globe's own structure is taken away within clear[0] units of the vortex (fading out to clear[1]) by a blur of clear[2] units, so the repaint closes the storm of the close image all the way round and the globe's small oval, which is that storm seen from far, does not stand beside it. bandPx: width and blur, in plate pixels, of the unfinished band along the border of the laid back image. finishedPx: blur under which the canvas is kept as it is. lock: the repaint keeps its own structure below lock[0] times the canvas blur (at least lock[1], at most lock[2] pixels) and takes the canvas above. lockGain: strength of the repaint's own structure. hiddenError: fixed point error of the lay back, in units, over which a place counts as hidden from the close image. feather: width of the join in units. nest: the near plate keeps its own repaint inside nest[0] units from its centre and is the mid plate beyond nest[1], measured with the power norm nestPower (a rounded square); the mid plate is the near plate made smaller inside the same shape.

image.note: The fit camera looks its own picture up: a point of the deck that the fit camera saw takes its colour from the canvas at the pixel where that camera saw it (deck/image.py writes the canvas, the core at twice its scale for the approved image, and the range the fit camera saw along every ray), so the frame at the fit pose is the approved image, and from any other pose every point keeps the colour it had. A point the fit camera did not see (farther along its ray than the stored range) takes the fill of the view chart. rangeShrink: canvas pixels per stored range, for the full and the web set. rangeLog2: the least and the greatest stored range as powers of two. hidden: a point counts as seen while it lies less than hidden[0] of the stored range beyond it, and as unseen from hidden[1]. sharpen: the footprint of a lookup in the canvas is taken this many times its true size. quality: of the stored pictures. march: slack, least step and hit distance in stored pixels, most steps, of the tool march. reach: units from the point under the fit camera beyond which the deck is the smooth sphere. steep: a point the fit camera saw so steeply that one pixel of the canvas is drawn over more than steep[0] pixels of the frame passes to the fill of the view chart, fully from steep[1] on; below that the canvas is shown as it is and the shader's own detail fills the scale it lacks.

tone.note: The tone of the approved view as a smooth field over the ground, written by assets-src/jupiter/plates/tone.py to deck-tone.bin (three stacked blocks of pixels x pixels, 16 bit, value times scale): the approved view laid on the ground over the plates, both blurred by blurUnits, carried out smoothly past the ground the view saw, and led back to 1 between the fade distances from the point under its camera. The plates are multiplied by it on both sides of the handover, so the ground the view saw and the ground beside it have one tone from above. known: the view counts fully within the first distance and not past the second. imageBlurPx: blur of the view before it is laid down. marginPx: rim of the canvas left out. range: least and most ratio. lift: the tone is off while the camera is lower than the first height in units over the deck and full from the second, so the surface view itself does not take it. rim: with the tone on, the approved view gives way to the toned plates between these two angles in degrees inside the edges of its canvas, so its footprint on the ground has no straight edge from above. rimNoise: two pairs of a wavelength in units and the degrees by which a value noise of the ground moves that edge.

above.note: How the ground looks from above the air, so the far field of the surface view's scene is the globe's far field at the handover. Knots lie evenly in the square root of the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground (0 at the horizon, 1 straight down). gain: the light of the ground is multiplied by it. air: light added on top, in the scene's own units before the exposure. Both act by the weight of air.lift (nothing under its first height, so frames 3060 to 3239 do not change). Measured at frame 3024 on stills of both sides: the globe alone (beauty/side=orbit/noplace) over the scene, medians per bin of the sine; under a sine of 0.2 the spread of the globe no longer follows the scene, so there the rest is added light.
